section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the same two categories exist in the aspects of world, place, and time, with the service of repentance transforming darkness into light, which is the unique quality of the Baal Teshuvah and the future redemption.
section.t: And likewise in the aspect of world,
place,
there are also these two matters.
For the world of Atzilus is clarified,

and the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, about which it is said “and from there it separates,” specifically in the world of separation, the world of Asiyah, the service is that of practical mitzvos.
And likewise Eretz Yisrael, upon which the eyes of Hashem are from the beginning of the year until the end of the year,
unlike the land of the nations, whose body is impure and whose air is impure,
behold, in order to make the land of the nations into Eretz Yisrael
there must be the greater service of “and her captives [shall be redeemed] with tzedakah.”
And likewise in the aspect of year,
time,
there are also these two types.
For in general, this is the distinction between the summer season and the winter season,
as explained elsewhere,
that in the summer season the service is easier than in the winter season,
for in the days of heat the sun shines,
and it is the aspect of the name Havayah,
(and the festivals in summer are more frequent).
And as it is brought in the Midrash,
“Because they go out from summer to winter… to a distant place… not in its season, to go and come.”
That is, the service in the winter season is distant,
more difficult than in the summer season.
And likewise is the distinction between the days of merit and days that are the opposite of merit.
For the service in the days of the opposite of merit is in the manner of “and her captives [shall be redeemed] with tzedakah,”
that Israel,
(through their service)
transform these days into joy and gladness,
in the future redemption that will come soon, literally.
And this matter,
(the transformation of these days into joy and gladness)
is accomplished specifically through the service of the line of teshuvah,
for the matter of teshuvah is the transformation of darkness into light,
for this is the advantage of the service of the Baal Teshuvah over the service of the righteous.
And this is also the connection of the future redemption specifically to the matter of teshuvah,
[that Israel does teshuvah,
(and specifically through this)
and immediately they are redeemed,
to the extent that the superiority of the future redemption
is that Mashiach comes to bring the righteous back in teshuvah],
for the innovation of the future redemption is the matter of transformation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse speaks of Torah and tzedakah as two general categories encompassing all aspects of world, year, and soul, and that redemption from exile requires service in all three lines, with Torah primarily redeeming Zion and tzedakah primarily redeeming the captives.
section.t: Based on the above, one can understand why this verse speaks only of the two matters of Torah
(judgment)
and tzedakah,
even though there are three lines,
for the intention in the matter of Torah
(judgment)
and tzedakah
(in this verse)
is for the two general categories within all the aspects of world, year, and soul,
(likewise, the matter of lights and vessels,
the name Havayah and the name Elokim, etc.).
And in each one, there must be service in all three lines.
For the redemption from exile
[in these matters
[masters of Torah and the righteous
(soul),
Eretz Yisrael
(world),
and days of merit
(year)]
their redemption from exile is in the manner of “Zion shall be redeemed with judgment”
(Torah)
“shall be redeemed.”
And in these matters
[masters of good deeds and Baalei Teshuvah,
the land of the nations,
and days that are the opposite of merit]
that their redemption is in the manner of “and her captives [shall be redeemed] with tzedakah,”
it is specifically through service in all three lines.
And as our sages, of blessed memory, said,
“Whoever engages in Torah, gemilus chasadim, and prays with the congregation… it is as if he redeemed me and my children from among the nations of the world,”
for the redemption of the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel from among the nations of the world is through service in all three lines,
(and in a congregational manner).
And as explained above regarding the aspect of Zion,
that this that Israel are the aspect of Zion is through their service in all three lines,
[and moreover,
through this that all three lines are in perfection].
And that which it says “Zion shall be redeemed with judgment”
(Torah)
“shall be redeemed” is because the redemption of the aspect of Zion
(in all three aspects of world, year, and soul)
is primarily through Torah,
likewise in the matter of “and her captives [shall be redeemed] with tzedakah,”
the redemption of the captives
(in all three aspects of world, year, and soul)
is specifically through service in all three lines.
And that which it says “and her captives [shall be redeemed] with tzedakah”
(specifically)
is because their redemption
(of the captives)
is primarily through tzedakah.
And additionally,
even in the matter of the mitzvos themselves
(for tzedakah is the entirety of the mitzvos,
as above)
there are all three lines,
the halachah in this, which is the matter of Torah,
the action in the physical object, which is the line of gemilus chasadim,
the elevation of the physical
(in which the mitzvah is performed)
which is the line of service,
for regarding offerings it is said “a pleasing aroma,” the aroma being the matter of elevation from below to above,
and likewise prayer,
(which corresponds to offerings)
about this it is said,
“A ladder set upon the earth and its head reaches the heavens.”
In addition to the known fact that in every mitzvah there are the three matters of thought, speech, and action, which are the three lines.
And based on the above, one can also understand the order of these three things
(in the aforementioned statement of our sages, of blessed memory),
Torah, gemilus chasadim, and prayer
(not in the usual order),
for in the general matter of “redeem me and my children from among the nations,” it is through engagement in Torah and gemilus chasadim,
“Zion shall be redeemed with judgment and her captives with tzedakah,”
except that in every matter
(and particularly in the matter of redemption from exile)
all three lines must be present,
“and prays with the congregation.”

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section concludes that the verse is set in the haftarah for the Shabbat before Tisha B'Av, reflecting G-d's healing before the blow, and that through Torah, tzedakah, and prayer, one achieves the redemption of the soul and the body and animal soul.
section.t: And this is “Zion shall be redeemed with judgment and her captives with tzedakah,”
that this verse is established in the haftarah of the Shabbat before Tisha B'Av
(for from Shabbat all the days are blessed,
including Tisha B'Av),
for this is analogous to the conduct of the Holy One, blessed be He, Who precedes the healing to the blow,
for His healing is in a manner that “from the outset I will not place [the blow] upon you,”
and through this one effects the redemption of each and every Jew, both in his soul and in his body and animal soul,
that the redemption of the soul is
(in general)
in the manner of “Zion shall be redeemed with judgment,”
and the redemption of the body and animal soul is in the manner of “and her captives [shall be redeemed] with tzedakah,”
[as is understood from what is explained in Tanya,
that the soul itself requires no rectification at all, and its descent below is only in order to rectify the body and animal soul].
And in order that Torah and tzedakah
(ascend above,
through which)
they effect actual redemption,
it is through prayer,
the line of service,
as above.
